title: The Weight Of Small Hours
subject: sitting up with someone who is ill
caption: Contemporary folk, almost entirely acoustic. Fingerpicked steel-string guitar in an open tuning, upright bass entering in the second verse, brushed percussion, a single cello line under the bridge. A soft male tenor sings barely above a whisper, extremely close-miked so the breath is audible, with a wordless female harmony joining the last chorus. Tape saturation, no reverb on the lead vocal, room tone left in. 74 BPM, C major. Tender, still, unsentimental.
lyrics:
[Intro - Fingerpicked Guitar]

[Verse 1]
The machine counts something out loud
Every four seconds, all night
I've started breathing along with it
Which I know is not useful

[Pre-Chorus]
You asked me once to stop fussing
So I'll just sit

[Chorus]
This is the weight of small hours
It isn't heavy, it's just long
I'd carry something heavier gladly
If anybody offered me the choice

[Verse 2]
The nurse has a good laugh
She uses it on purpose
She knows exactly what it's for
And it works, it works on me

[Cello - Bridge]

[Chorus - with harmony]
This is the weight of small hours
It isn't heavy, it's just long
I'd carry something heavier gladly
If anybody offered me the choice

[Outro]
Just long
Just long
